findings.body: Reload initialization sets `enabled` to false before awaiting the downstream refresh (`register.ts:32`), which can wait on Forge processes for up to twenty seconds. If the active main turn completes during that wait, the completion handler skips clearing its persisted active-turn id because `enabled` is false. Once initialization finishes, every refresh sees that stale id at line 67 and leaves new occurrences pending indefinitely, until another user turn completes. A turn starting during initialization is likewise omitted from tracking. New evidence beyond the previous reload finding is this initialization gap introduced by the persistent busy-state fix: both reload tests await `session.start` before completing the main turn. The [pinned lifecycle contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/684800b206824dfd0cc8a876e8604b20f72c3617/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts) distinguishes the awaited first start from later reload notifications. Keep main-turn tracking active while the reload refresh awaits, and cover completion during that refresh.
findings.title: Not done: track active turns throughout reload initialization

findings.body: The previous test-routing gap remains open. `forge.toml:6` and the current workflows run pytest; `tests/test_mod_plugin.py:45–57` only typecheck the native TypeScript tests. The expanded packaged test now covers busy reload batching, but failed-submit retries, worker/headless gating and session-reset behavior still rely on native assertions that the repository suite does not execute. SHIP owns the plugin CI job (`plans/FORGE-MOD-1.md:284`), so that task must route these tests into automated checks.
